native.answer:
Slow, deep breathing helps calm nerves through a few interconnected physiological mechanisms. Firstly, it activates the parasympathetic nervous system – often called the “rest and digest” system – which counteracts the “fight or flight” response triggered by stress. 

When we’re stressed, our breathing becomes faster and shallower, signaling danger to the body. This leads to increased heart rate, muscle tension, and release of stress hormones like cortisol. Slow, deep breaths signal safety.

Deep breathing increases oxygen levels in the blood, which can have a calming effect. It also physically slows the heart rate and lowers blood pressure. The act of focusing on the breath itself can also be a form of mindfulness, diverting attention away from anxious thoughts and bringing you into the present moment. Essentially, it’s a way to physiologically “tell” your body it’s safe, even if your mind is still racing.
